objectives_explanation: D1 and D2 both choose A+B+C. The deterministic NPV (SAR 1,563,087) is below the expected NPV (SAR 2,557,033) because the deterministic case uses most-likely values while the tariff range is skewed upwards (mode 0.18, mean 0.207 SAR/kWh); at mean inputs the deterministic optimum is A+B+C (NPV SAR 2,546,316).

With fixed reporting factors, A+B meets the target in 93.69% of the 20,000 scenarios and 93.52% on an independent validation sample of 200,000 (95% CI 93.41%-93.63%), above 90%. The validated carbon rule D3 chooses A+B+C, which has a higher expected NPV among the portfolios that pass.
